paragraphs: R’ Papias (a Tanna of the Mishnah).

Eduyot [7:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Eduyot.7.6)–[7:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Eduyot.7.7) and [Temurah 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Temurah.3.1) record his testimony with R’ Yehoshua. Hyman cites “there, 6:5” for another testimony by Papias.
Likewise in [Nazir ch. 3 mishnah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Nazir.3.2) he testified concerning one who took two nazirite vows, etc.
In [Shekalim 4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Shekalim.4.7) he says: “I heard rulings agreeing with both of them”—Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.
Hyman cites [Beitzah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29b.2) for a disagreement between Papias and R’ Yehudah ben Beteira.[^4]

Hyman also cites [Sanhedrin 94a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.94a.9), the Mekhilta, Yitro, tractate Amalek, chapter 1, and the beginning of Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 26 (the corresponding teaching is at [27:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Avot_DeRabbi_Natan.27.2)).
And we find R’ Tima ben Papias in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, chapter 4, halakhah 1 as cited by Hyman (the named passage is at [4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.4.7.4)).[^5]

notes.text: The checked Shekalim explicitly names Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua; this expansion is not an automatic choice for every ר״א. Temurah 3:1 and Eduyot 7:6–7 contain Papias’s testimonies. The supplied “there, 6:5” remains unresolved: Eduyot 6:5 was unavailable and Temurah 6:5 does not name him.

No new primary scalar was returned. The older Shekalim/Eduyot/Temurah comparisons remain inherited, not newly inspected whole texts. Later saved chapter6 fetches supersede the blanket Eduyot-unavailable claim but do not settle there6:5 or authorize renumbering from a snippet. The original note’s שיעיד does not occur in the supplied source and is withdrawn as a rationale; all source questions remain. TWO nazirite vows and BOTH rulings remain. רפ״כו means BEGINNING chapter26, not end. Sanhedrin94 has no supplied amud; Yitro/tractateAmalek and Tima4:1 remain literal. No global full-title transfer follows from the earlier local Shekalim expansion.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. III, p. 1032) gives “there, 6:5.” In the consulted editions, Eduyot 7:6 and Temurah 3:1 name Papias and R’ Yehoshua for the testimony on the offspring of a peace offering, and Eduyot 7:7 continues with further testimony. Eduyot 7:5 gives Papias’s other testimony, on two nazirite vows, also recorded in Nazir 3:2. These passages attest a second testimony by Papias independently of the historical citation. The exact source behind Hyman’s “6:5” remains uncertain: the consulted Eduyot chapter 6 has three units, and Temurah 6:5 addresses another case. At Beitzah 29b the consulted baraita gives Papias and R’ Yehudah ben Beteira’s permission to sift flour a second time jointly. Sanhedrin 94a names Papias, and the horse teaching in the consulted Avot de-Rabbi Natan appears in chapter 27. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud places Tima bar Papias in Sanhedrin 4:7, speaking in Rav Hoshaya’s name. Hyman’s Mekhilta citation and historical chapter numbering remain uncollated.

The linked Beitzah passage attributes the permission to sift flour a second time to both Papias and Yehudah ben Beteira. [Heilprin’s Papias entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3001&lang=en) also gives both names. Papias’s testimony about two nazirite vows appears in [Eduyot 7:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Eduyot.7.5) as well as Nazir 3:2. The source Hyman cites as “there, 6:5” remains uncertain.

The linked Yerushalmi passage has Tima bar Papias speaking in the name of Rav Hoshaya about the order in which judges speak. See also [Heilprin’s cross-reference for Tima](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3567&lang=en).
